name: Urban Suite - Path Dependence
catalogPath: Curricular Models/Urban Suite/Urban Suite - Path Dependence
miniText: The scientific question is whether early settlement events shape the eventual clustering of firms. In NetLogo's Urban Suite - Path Dependence model, mobile firms probabilistically settle according to local quality and the number of firms already present, with alternative decision mechanisms. The selected literature connects this mechanism to historical contingency and spatial concentration: increasing returns explain persistent outcomes selected by historical events [1]; urban complexity models situate firm-location feedback in spatial systems [2]; reinforcement offers a comparator for uneven cumulative growth [3]. Location probabilities encode assumptions about agglomeration rather than estimating them; alternative random histories need ensembles before conclusions about lock-in. The original NetLogo behavior is the baseline for reimplementation. This simulation offers a controlled thought experiment, and agreement with its output does not establish empirical validation.

modelSource.citation: For the model itself: * Rand, W. and Wilensky, U. (2007). NetLogo Urban Suite - Path Dependence model. http://ccl.northwestern.edu/netlogo/models/UrbanSuite-PathDependence. Center for Connected Learning and Computer-Based Modeling, Northwestern University, Evanston, IL.
modelSource.scientificOrigin: This model is loosely based on the model presented in this paper: Arthur, W.B. (1988), "Urban systems and historical path dependence", in Ausubel, J.H., Herman, R. (Eds), Cities and their Vital Systems: Infrastructure, Past, Present and Future, National Academy Press, Washington, DC, pp.85-97. Thanks to Bill Rand for his work on this model. The Urban Suite models were developed as part of the Procedural Modeling of Cities project, under the sponsorship of NSF ITR award 0326542, Electronic Arts & Maxis. Please see the project web site ( http://ccl.northwestern.edu/cities/ ) for more information.
modelSource.notes: This is source research, not runtime execution or approval of the City Library reimplementation. Original model notices remain in the retained source.
